Installation: - Use the eva_ramboot.py script to load the initramfs image on the device. Run it a few seconds after turning the device on. If it fails to find the device try the ip address 169.254.120.1 (Firmware updates or the recovery tool apparently change it).\\ <code>
**IMPORTANT:** Set lzma compression in ramdisk options, bootloader stalls when receiving uncompressed images.
- The device will load the initramfs image in RAM and boot it.
- After booting the initramfs image, you can reach it under the OpenWrt default ip address 192.168.1.1.
- Run sysupgrade to persistently install OpenWrt.

Note: The first boot may take a bit longer than usual. This happens if the TFFS variable ''linux_fs_start'' is set to 1. In that case the bootloader will initially try to boot the second system image, which is no longer valid after installation of OpenWrt. Eventually, it should fall back to 0 though, and it should then boot normally. (If you want to check the current ''linux_fs_start'' value from OpenWrt, you can use the command ''fritz_tffs -n linux_fs_start -i /dev/mtd3''. To change the variable manually, you would need to connect to the bootloader via FTP with login/password adam2 and issue the command ''quote SETENV linux_fs_start 0''.)

openwrt_git_support.titel: lantiq: add basic support for AVM FRITZ!Box 3390
openwrt_git_support.nachricht:
lantiq: add basic support for AVM FRITZ!Box 3390

The FRITZ!Box 3390 actually contains two SoCs, one Lantiq with a
5GHz WiFi and one AR9342 with a 2.4GHz WiFi. Only the Lantiq
has access to the flash memory, the Atheros runs fully from RAM.

Specifications
--------------

  - Lantiq 500 MHz
  - 128MiB RAM
  - 128MiB NAND
  - 256k Flash
  - AR9580 5GHz WiFi
  - AR9342 560 MHz
  - 64MiB RAM
  - AR9328 2.4GHz WiFi

Remarks
-------

This commit only adds support for the Lantiq side of things and
prepares the drivers for communication with the Atheros SoC. Thus,
only 5GHz WiFi works by default, the 2.4GHz WiFi will be added via
another target.

Some kernel patches will be required to add support for the Atheros SoC.

Installation
------------

Use the eva_ramboot.py script to boot the initramfs image. Then, transfer
the sysupgrade image to the device and run sysupgrade to flash it to the
NAND.

Signed-off-by: Andreas Böhler <dev@aboehler.at>
Acked-by: Aleksander Jan Bajkowski A.Bajkowski@stud.elka.pw.edu.pl
Signed-off-by: Joachim Cerny <cocktail_yogi@web.de>
